data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":["SRC_002"],"disanalogies":["The ablation test is a single-run diagnostic, while population statistics require multiple runs.","The ablation test operates on the causal mechanism, not on the statistical properties of the engine."],"overturn_conditions":["An engine produces a perturbation-sensitive checking trace but is shown to be restating a false execution result it generated itself.","The ablation test is shown to be gameable by an engine that anticipates the perturbation."],"shared_structure":["Both claims and execution results can be verified by observing sensitivity to perturbation.","Both involve a causal link between the evidence and the verdict.","Both can be tested by replacing the evidence with a counterfactual."],"source_memory_refs":["SCR_002"],"transfer_claims":["The ablation test for causal sensitivity in execution verification transfers to counting verification: replace the count with count\u00b11 and observe if the verdict flips.","The operational definition of verification as perturbation-sensitivity transfers from scientific measurement to LLM verification."]},"claim":"Separating the authoring and checking engines is not necessary; genuine independent verification is achieved within a single run when the verdict is causally sensitive to the execution or counting result.
